title: EvoTest: Evolutionary Test-Time Learning for Self-Improving Agentic Systems
claim: A system improves itself at test time by looping between acting on a task and evolving its whole configuration from its own trajectory.
layout: 2 stacked parts: top timeline, bottom Act/Evolve boxes; left-to-right with feedback loop
description: The figure has two parts. The top is a dashed box with a timeline of repeated episodes. A robot labeled LOSE appears at Episode 1 and Episode 2, and an ape-to-human evolution icon sits between them for the Evolve steps. Ellipsis dots lead to a final robot labeled WIN with stars at Episode k. The bottom has two solid boxes. The left box, Act Phase, shows an agent configuration card (prompt, memory, hyperparameters, tool-use). Below it, an Environment (game screen and controller) exchanges state, reward and action with the Actor Agent. This produces a trajectory transcript card. Green arrows carry the transcript to the right box, Evolve Phase. There, an Evolver Agent combines a system prompt, all previous configurations and UCB-based selection to produce a new agent configuration. A green arrow loops that back to the Act phase. The colors are pastel green, blue and yellow cards, with cartoon icons.
caption: The EvoTest architecture, designed to enable test-time learning (TTL). The agent operates in a continuous Act-Evolve loop across multiple attempts at the same task. After each episode, the Evolver Agent analyzes the full trajectory transcript—rich narrative feedback to perform gradient-free, whole-system evolution on the agent's entire configuration. This allows the agentic system to self-improve on the fly, directly from its own experience at test time.
abstract: A fundamental limitation of current AI agents is their inability to learn complex skills on the fly at test time, often behaving like "clever but clueless interns" in novel environments. This severely limits their practical utility. To systematically measure and drive progress on this challenge, we first introduce the Jericho Test-Time Learning (J-TTL) benchmark. J-TTL is a new evaluation setup where an agent must play the same game for several consecutive episodes, attempting to improve its performance from one episode to the next. On J-TTL, we find that existing adaptation methods like reflection, memory, or reinforcement learning struggle. To address the challenges posed by our benchmark, we present EvoTest, an evolutionary test-time learning framework that improves an agent without any fine-tuning or gradients-by evolving the entire agentic system after every episode. EvoTest has two roles: the Actor Agent, which plays the game, and the Evolver Agent, which analyzes the episode transcript to propose a revised configuration for the next run. This configuration rewrites the prompt, updates memory by logging effective state-action choices, tunes hyperparameters, and learns the tool-use routines. On our J-TTL benchmark, EvoTest consistently increases performance, outperforming not only reflection and memory-only baselines but also more complex online fine-tuning methods. Notably, our method is the only one capable of winning two games (Detective and Library), while all baselines fail to win any.
